atoms.text: Now Sally is going to fly you around some of her favourite cliffs and rocks.

instruction.text: What is a cliff? Select the grass to learn more.

feedback.end: Great! A cliff is a steep rock face. Cliffs are often found by the sea, because waves have broken away the rest of the land. They are another example of physical geography on our coastlines.

instruction.text: This is Durdle Door in Dorset. Select the arch to learn more.

feedback.end: Great! Durdle Door is a very famous natural arch. The hole was once filled with a softer rock than the rest of the cliff, but it was removed by waves over time.

instruction.text: Let’s do some fieldwork! Find different locations on the map.

hint.text: Use the plus and minus buttons to zoom in on the map.

instruction.text: You are at Hardy Cliffs with Sally. Answer Sally’s questions.

atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>Which direction is Torr Beach</voice>
ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>Which direction are Handfast Rocks</voice>
ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='f14'>Which direction is Warren Wood</voice>

instruction.text: These are Old Harry’s Rocks in Dorset. Select one of the rocks to learn more.

feedback.end: Just like at Durdle Door, waves have removed the softer rock from a cliff and left behind these stacks of harder rock.
